Italian sea platform off Kenya that launched Uhuru, the first satellite dedicated to X-ray astronomy

Facts from the Wikipedia articles on the Broglio Space Center, the San Marco programme, Uhuru and the Scout rocket family. Coordinates are the San Marco platform position on English Wikipedia (2 56 18 S, 40 12 45 E). OpenStreetMap maps three platforms within 700 m of it but labels them differently, so which one is San Marco is not settled. The platform was run by the University of Rome's Aerospace Research Centre (CRA) under an agreement with NASA; the Italian Space Agency (ASI) has managed the site since 2004.
Centro spaziale Luigi Broglio di Malindi — ASI

San Marco was a launch platform in the Indian Ocean off Ras Ngomeni, near Malindi, Kenya, about 3 degrees south of the equator, where an eastward launch gets the most help from Earth's rotation. A former oil platform, it was run by the University of Rome's Aerospace Research Centre under a 1962 agreement with NASA; a second platform, Santa Rita, housed launch control, and a smaller one the radar. NASA supplied Scout rockets and trained the Italian crews. San Marco 2 flew from here on 26 April 1967, the first satellite launched from a sea platform. Uhuru, the first satellite dedicated to X-ray astronomy, followed on 12 December 1970 on a Scout B. The last satellite, San Marco D/L, flew in March 1988. ASI has managed the centre since 2004, and its ground station still tracks satellites.
